question:
A three-digit code has hundreds digit $x$, tens digit $y$, and units digit $z$. The sum of its digits is $12$, the hundreds digit exceeds the units digit by $2$, and twice the hundreds digit plus the tens digit minus the units digit is $11$. Since each digit must be determined simultaneously, the conditions are expressed as a system of three linear equations and solved using the inverse-matrix method.

(a) Form the system and express it as $AX=B$.

(b) Calculate $|A|$ and determine whether the code is uniquely determined.

(c) Find $A^{-1}$ and hence determine $x$, $y$, and $z$.

(d) Form the code and calculate the difference between the code and the number obtained by reversing its digits.
explanation:
(a)
The conditions give
$$x+y+z=12$$
$$x-z=2$$
$$2x+y-z=11$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 0 & -1\\2 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}12\\2\\11\end{bmatrix}$$

(b)
$$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\1 & 0 & -1\\2 & 1 & -1\end{vmatrix}$$
$$=1(1)-1(1)+1(1)=1$$
Since $|A|=1\neq0$, the system has a unique solution and the code is uniquely determined.

(c)
The inverse of the coefficient matrix is
$$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 & -1\\-1 & -3 & 2\\1 & 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix}=A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}12\\2\\11\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\begin{bmatrix}12+4-11\\-12-6+22\\12+2-11\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5\\4\\3\end{bmatrix}$$
Thus,
$$x=5,\quad y=4,\quad z=3$$

(d)
The required code is $543$. The number obtained by reversing its digits is $345$. Therefore,
$$543-345=198$$
Hence, the difference is $198$.

options.A:
(a) $x+y+z=12,\ x-z=2,\ 2x+y-z=11$
(b) $|A|=1$, so the code is unique
(c) $A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&-1\\-1&-3&2\\1&1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $(x,y,z)=(5,4,3)$
(d) Code $543$, reversed number $345$, difference $198$
options.C:
(a) $x+y+z=12,\ x-z=2,\ 2x+y-z=11$
(b) $|A|=0$, so the code is not unique
(c) $(x,y,z)=(5,4,3)$
(d) Code $543$, difference $198$
